knowledge:
- key_parameters: gaps=A data frame or GRanges object containing chromosome coordinates, lengths, and centromere positions (e.g., hg_gap or mm10_gap) ;; bands=A data frame or GRanges object containing cytoband information (e.g., hg_cytoBandIdeo) or genomic elements to plot directly on the chromosome body ;; annot1, annot2, annot3, annot4=Genomic data tracks plotted as histograms or genomic elements ;; segment, segment2=Large genomic segments (e.g., QTLs, ancestry blocks) plotted as vertical bars ;; stat, stat2=Genomic elements associated with continuous numeric values for XY plotting ;; statCol, statCol2=The column name containing continuous values in the stat/stat2 objects ;; statTyp=The plot type for statistics ("p" for points, "l" for lines, "n" for no points/labels only) ;; chr=A character vector specifying which chromosomes to display ;; figCols=An integer specifying the number of columns in the output figure grid ;; chrSide=A numeric vector of 1 (left) or -1 (right) specifying the side of the chromosome for each data track ;; noHist=A logical value; if TRUE, prevents automatic conversion of segments/annotations to histograms ;; stack=A logical value; if TRUE, stacks non-overlapping segments to save space ;; statSumm=A character string specifying a statistical function (e.g., "mean", "median", "sum", "none") to apply to binned data ;; legChrom=An integer or character specifying the chromosome under which to place the legend, or NA to omit it ;; org=An organism name (e.g., "hsapiens") to retrieve Ensembl genes via biomaRt if annot1 is not provided
- alternatives: biomaRt=Used to retrieve gene annotations remotely when org is specified ;; GenomicFeatures/TxDb=Used to extract transcripts and genomic coordinates locally ;; qtl=Used to perform QTL mapping and generate LOD scores before plotting
- when_to_use: Use this package when you need to visualize multiple heterogeneous genomic data types (such as gene density, QTL regions, selection signals like Fst/iHS, and synteny) simultaneously across whole chromosomes in a single publication-quality figure.
- pitfalls: Continuous variables with too many distinct colors can be hard to distinguish; users should bin continuous data and assign colors to bins manually ;; Small segments or large datasets automatically convert to histograms unless noHist=TRUE is explicitly set ;; Automatic legend placement can sometimes overlap data; use legChrom to shift the legend to a different chromosome or set it to NA and use the manual legend() function ;; The statSumm argument does not perform sanity checks on the function name provided, so users must ensure the function is valid and appropriate for their data ;; Wrong color names in a custom 'Colors' column will cause R to throw errors.

workflows.name: idiogram_and_synteny_mapping
workflows.intent: Plot chromosome idiograms (G-banding) and highlight genomic elements or synteny blocks directly on the chromosome body.
input: hg_gap (UCSC gap track data frame)
hg_cytoBandIdeo (UCSC cytoband data frame)
refGeneHg (data frame of genomic elements with Chrom, Start, End, and optional Colors/Group columns)
sinteny (data frame of syntenic regions with Chrom, Start, End, and Group columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Load coordinate gaps and cytoband data ;; 2. Plot basic chromosome structures ;; 3. Plot G-banding patterns ;; 4. Overlay genomic elements or synteny blocks on the chromosome body
workflows.code:
chromPlot(gaps=hg_gap)
chromPlot(bands=hg_cytoBandIdeo, gaps=hg_gap, chr=c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"), figCols=6)
chromPlot(gaps=hg_gap, bands=refGeneHg, chr=c(19, 20, 21), figCols=3)
chromPlot(gaps=hg_gap, bands=sinteny, chr=c(19:21), figCols=3)

workflows.name: histogram_density_profiling
workflows.intent: Plot single or stacked density histograms of genomic features (such as transcripts or differentially expressed genes) on the sides of chromosomes.
input: hg_gap (UCSC gap track data frame)
txgr (GRanges object of transcripts)
refGeneHg (data frame of reference genes)
ref_mm10 (data frame of mouse reference genes)
array (data frame of array-represented genes)
DEneg (data frame of down-regulated genes)
DEpos (data frame of up-regulated genes)
monocytes (data frame of categorized differentially expressed genes)
workflows.stages: 1. Load coordinate gaps and cytobands ;; 2. Extract or load genomic features ;; 3. Plot single track density histograms ;; 4. Plot stacked histograms representing multiple filtering stages (e.g., reference genes vs. array genes vs. differentially expressed genes) ;; 5. Plot stacked histograms categorized by a single grouping variable
workflows.code:
chromPlot(gaps=hg_gap, annot1=txgr)
chromPlot(gaps=hg_gap, bands=hg_cytoBandIdeo, annot1=refGeneHg, chr=c(19:21), figCols=3)
chromPlot(gaps=mm10_gap, bands=mm10_cytoBandIdeo, annot1=ref_mm10, annot2=array, annot3=DEneg, annot4=DEpos, chr=c( "17", "18", "19"), figCols=3, chrSide=c(-1, -1, -1, 1, -1, 1, -1, 1), noHist=FALSE)
chromPlot(gaps=hg_gap, bands=hg_cytoBandIdeo, annot1=refGeneHg, segment=monocytes, chrSide=c(-1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1), figCols=3, chr=c(19:21))

workflows.name: xy_plotting_of_genomic_statistics
workflows.intent: Plot continuous genomic statistics (such as Fst, iHS, XP-EHH, or LOD scores) along chromosomes as points or lines, with optional thresholding and summarization.
input: hg_gap (UCSC gap track data frame)
hg_cytoBandIdeo (UCSC cytoband data frame)
fst (data frame of Fst values with Chrom, Start, End, and win.FST columns)
ihs (data frame of iHS values with Chrom, Start, End, and iHS columns)
xpehh (data frame of XP-EHH values with Chrom, Start, End, XP, and ID columns)
QTLs (data frame of LOD scores with Chrom, Start, and LOD columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Load coordinate gaps and cytobands ;; 2. Plot continuous statistics as points or lines ;; 3. Apply bin-level summarization (e.g., mean) to smooth the plot ;; 4. Plot multiple continuous tracks simultaneously with thresholds and text labels for specific data points ;; 5. Plot LOD curves from QTL mapping along with gene density
workflows.code:
chromPlot(bands=hg_cytoBandIdeo, gaps=hg_gap, stat=fst, statCol="win.FST", statName="win.FST", statTyp="p", chr=c(19:21), figCols=3, scex=0.7, spty=20, statSumm="none")
chromPlot(bands=hg_cytoBandIdeo, gaps=hg_gap, stat=fst, statCol="win.FST", statName="win.FST", statTyp="p", chr=c(19:21), figCols=3, scex=0.7, spty=20, statSumm="mean")
chromPlot(bands=hg_cytoBandIdeo, gaps=hg_gap, stat=fst, statCol="win.FST", statName="win.FST", statTyp="l", chr=c(19:21), figCols=3, statSumm="none")
chromPlot(bands=hg_cytoBandIdeo, gaps=hg_gap, stat=fst, statCol="win.FST", statName="win.FST", statTyp="l", chr=c(19:21), figCols=3, statSumm="mean")
chromPlot(gaps=hg_gap, bands=fst, stat=ihs, stat2=xpehh, statCol="iHS", statCol2="XP", statName="iHS", statName2="normxpehh", colStat="red", colStat2="blue", statTyp="p", scex=2, spty=20, statThreshold=1.2, statThreshold2=1.5, chr=c(19:21), bin=1e6, figCols=3, cex=0.7, statSumm="none", legChrom=19, stack=FALSE)
chromPlot(gaps=mm10_gap, bands=mm10_cytoBandIdeo, annot1=ref_mm10, stat=QTLs, statCol="LOD", chrSide=c(-1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1), statTyp="l", chr=c(2,17:18), figCols=3)

workflows.name: segment_and_ancestry_mapping
workflows.intent: Plot large genomic segments (such as QTL intervals, ancestry blocks, or phenotype associations) as vertical bars on the sides of chromosomes, categorized by one or two grouping variables.
input: mm10_gap (UCSC gap track data frame)
mm10_cytoBandIdeo (UCSC cytoband data frame)
qtl (data frame of QTL segments with Chrom, Start, End, and Group columns)
ref_mm10 (data frame of mouse reference genes)
pheno_ancestry (data frame of SNP associations with Chrom, Start, End, Group, and Group2 columns)
ancestry (data frame of ancestry blocks with Chrom, Start, End, and Group columns)
region (data frame of donor regions with Chrom, Start, End, and Colors columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Load coordinate gaps and cytobands ;; 2. Plot large stacked segments on the side of the chromosome body ;; 3. Plot segments grouped by two categories (using color for Group and shape for Group2) ;; 4. Plot non-overlapping categorized genomic regions (e.g., ancestry blocks) ;; 5. Integrate multiple data types (e.g., donor regions on the chromosome body, gene density on the left, and QTL segments on the right)
workflows.code:
chromPlot(gaps=mm10_gap, segment=qtl, noHist=TRUE, annot1=ref_mm10, chrSide=c(-1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1), chr=c(2,11,17), stack=TRUE, figCol=3, bands=mm10_cytoBandIdeo)
chromPlot(bands=hg_cytoBandIdeo, gaps=hg_gap, segment=pheno_ancestry, noHist=TRUE, chr=c(3:5), figCols=3, legChrom=5)
chromPlot(gaps=hg_gap, bands=hg_cytoBandIdeo, chrSide=c(-1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1), noHist=TRUE, annot1=refGeneHg, figCols=3, segment=ancestry, colAnnot1="blue", chr=c(19:21), legChrom=21)
chromPlot(gaps=mm10_gap, segment=qtl, noHist=TRUE, annot1=ref_mm10, chrSide=c(-1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1), chr=c(2,11,17), stack=TRUE, figCol=3, bands=region, colAnnot1="blue")
